findings.quote: the highest since the conflict began in late February
findings.why: Context has higher Brent prints in the same window than the $108 cited: Morgan Stanley's 'Fundamentals offer little relief' piece logs Brent Crude Oil (Europe spot) at $114.89 on 2026-09-22, and its 'Cross-Asset Spotlight' piece has Brent touching $110/bbl intraday 'last week' -- both above $108, so the superlative isn't supported by the rest of the context.
findings.fix: Drop the "highest since" superlative, or attribute it explicitly as SEB/Danske Bank's own characterization rather than an established fact.

findings.quote: Saudi Arabia has pushed crude exports back up to 3.6 million barrels a day this month from just 900,000 in August, ship-tracking data show
findings.why: The Kpler-sourced data point in context has figure_status "forecast" and reads "Saudi crude exports via Hormuz were on track to rebound to 3.6 million barrels per day in September" -- a projected trajectory, not a completed move as the draft states it.
findings.fix: Reword to "is on track to push crude exports back up to" rather than stating the rebound as already accomplished.

findings.quote: Daily oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have collapsed to 4.9 million barrels a day this year from 21.2 million in 2025 (JPMorgan)
findings.why: JPMorgan's data point specifies "Average barrels per day in Q2 2026" ("fell to 4.9 million in the second quarter of this year"), not a full-year 2026 figure as "this year" implies.
findings.fix: Say "in the second quarter" instead of "this year" to match JPMorgan's actual period.

findings.quote: a real deal still flips this to a relief rally in energy and small caps
findings.why: JPMorgan's bull case in context is "A deal this week leads to a short squeeze rally with RTY leading as energy prices collapse" -- the rally is in equities/small caps while energy prices fall, not a rally in energy itself as the draft states.
findings.fix: Say the deal scenario flips this to a rally in small caps as energy prices fall, not a rally "in energy."
